In the llama.cpp repo at /home/nick/work/llama.cpp, find the EXACT calling convention for ggml vec_dot kernels when nrc (num rows) == 2. READ-ONLY.
1. In ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c find where mul_mat calls vec_dot with num_rows_per_vec_dot possibly > 1 - quote the exact call with the bs/bx/by arguments and their values, with file:line.
2. Find ONE existing kernel that implements nrc == 2 (search ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/ for "nrc == 2", e.g. arm or x86 q4_0/q8_0) and show exactly how it addresses the second row (vx + bx?) and writes the two results (s[0] and s[bs]? s[1]? units in floats or bytes) with file:line.
3. In ggml-cpu.c, show how the .nrows field of type_traits_cpu is set per-architecture (exact #if defined(...) examples with line numbers), and where num_rows_per_vec_dot is decided in mul_mat (any conditions like even row count, src types).
4. Note how odd/tail rows are handled when nrows=2.
Be precise - this defines an ABI a new kernel must match. Quote code, do not paraphrase.

input.caller: ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c:1265 (inside ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat_one_chunk): `vec_dot(ne00, &tmp[ir0 - iir0], (num_rows_per_vec_dot > 1 ? 16 : 0), src0_row + ir0 * nb01, (num_rows_per_vec_dot > 1 ? nb01 : 0), src1_col, (num_rows_per_vec_dot > 1 ? src1_col_stride : 0), num_rows_per_vec_dot);` where src1_col_stride is defined at line 1227: `const size_t src1_col_stride = src1_cont || src1->type != vec_dot_type ? row_size : nb11;` (row_size = ggml_row_size(vec_dot_type, ne10), line 1218). Note BOTH loops step by num_rows_per_vec_dot: the ir1 (src1 column) loop at line 1235 and the ir0 (src0 row) loop at line 1264 - so one nrc=2 call computes a 2x2 tile. Results go to a local `float tmp[32]` (line 1231, comment "16 * 2, accounting for mmla kernels"), then lines 1268-1270 copy out: `for (int cn = 0; cn < num_rows_per_vec_dot; ++cn) { memcpy(&dst_col[iir0 + cn * nb1 / nb0], tmp + (cn * 16), (MIN(iir0 + blck_0, ir0_end) - iir0) * sizeof(float)); }` - i.e. tmp[0..15] holds results for src1 column j=0, tmp[16..31] for column j=1.
input.convention: Signature (e.g. ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/arm/quants.c:297): `void ggml_vec_dot_q4_0_q8_0(int n, float * s, size_t bs, const void * vx, size_t bx, const void * vy, size_t by, int nrc)`. For nrc==2: n = ne00 (element count of one row, in elements not blocks). s = output pointer into a float buffer; bs = output stride in FLOAT ELEMENTS (caller always passes 16), NOT bytes - the kernel must write a 2x2 tile as s[j*bs + i] = dot(src0 row i, src1 col j): s[0]=x0.y0, s[1]=x1.y0, s[bs]=x0.y1, s[bs+1]=x1.y1. vx = first src0 row (quantized blocks); bx = BYTE stride to the second src0 row (caller passes nb01, the src0 row byte stride); second row is at (const uint8_t*)vx + bx. vy = first src1 column (in vec_dot_type, e.g. q8_0 blocks); by = BYTE stride to the second src1 column (caller passes src1_col_stride = row_size or nb11); second column is at (const uint8_t*)vy + by. For nrc==1 the caller passes bs=0, bx=0, by=0 and the kernel writes only *s.
input.example_kernel: ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/arm/quants.c:297-386, ggml_vec_dot_q4_0_q8_0, `#if defined(__ARM_FEATURE_MATMUL_INT8)` block starting `if (nrc == 2) {` at line 316. Second row/col addressing (lines 317-320): `const block_q4_0 * vx1 = (const block_q4_0 *) ((const uint8_t*)vx + bx);` and `const block_q8_0 * vy1 = (const block_q8_0 *) ((const uint8_t*)vy + by);` - bx/by are byte offsets. Per-block scales are ordered {x0*y0, x0*y1, x1*y0, x1*y1} (lines 354-359) matching the vmmlaq_s32 2x2 output lanes. Result write (lines 378-382): `float32x4_t sumv1 = vextq_f32(sumv0, sumv0, 2); float32x4_t sumv2 = vzip1q_f32(sumv0, sumv1); vst1_f32(s, vget_low_f32(sumv2)); vst1_f32(s + bs, vget_high_f32(sumv2));` - this permutes lanes [x0y0,x0y1,x1y0,x1y1] into [x0y0,x1y0,x0y1,x1y1], so s[0]=x0.y0, s[1]=x1.y0 (float index, both rows for y col 0) and s[bs]=x0.y1, s[bs+1]=x1.y1 (y col 1). `s + bs` is pointer arithmetic on float*, confirming bs is in float elements.
input.nrows_traits:
ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c, table `static const struct ggml_type_traits_cpu type_traits_cpu[GGML_TYPE_COUNT]` starting at line 236. nrows=2 is gated only on `__ARM_FEATURE_MATMUL_INT8` (ARM i8mm); every other arch (x86 included) uses 1. Exact examples: GGML_TYPE_Q4_0 lines 265-269: `#if defined (__ARM_FEATURE_MATMUL_INT8)
 .nrows = 2,
#else
 .nrows = 1,
#endif`. Same pattern for GGML_TYPE_Q4_1 (lines 275-279), GGML_TYPE_Q8_0 (lines 297-301), GGML_TYPE_Q4_K (lines 336-340), GGML_TYPE_Q6_K (lines 352-356). All other types (F32, F16, Q1_0, Q2_0, Q5_0, Q5_1, Q8_1, MXFP4, NVFP4, Q2_K, Q3_K, Q5_K, IQ*) have unconditional `.nrows = 1`. Read into mul_mat at line 1296: `int64_t const vec_dot_num_rows = type_traits_cpu[src0->type].nrows;` (indexed by src0->type; the vec_dot_type, e.g. Q8_0, is a separate field).
input.row_pairing: Decision in ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat, ggml-cpu.c:1458-1465: `int64_t num_rows_per_vec_dot = vec_dot_num_rows;` then `if ((nr0 % 2 != 0) || (ne11 % 2 != 0) || ((ir0_end - ir0_start) % 2 != 0) || ((ir1_end - ir1_start) % 2 != 0)) { num_rows_per_vec_dot = 1; }` where nr0 = ne0 (total dst/src0 rows) and ne11 = src1 columns. So nrc=2 is used only when: src0 row count is even, src1 column count (ne11) is even, AND this thread's chunk ranges in both dims are even-sized. There is NO per-call tail handling: any odd count anywhere makes the ENTIRE chunk fall back to nrc=1, one row/col per call. A new nrc=2 kernel therefore never sees an odd remainder - it can assume exactly 2 rows and 2 columns per call - but it MUST still implement the nrc==1 path (kernels assert `(nrc == 2) || (nrc == 1)`, e.g. arm/quants.c:303), since the fallback calls the same function with nrc=1, bs=bx=by=0. Pairing is always adjacent: rows ir0 and ir0+1 (vx, vx+nb01) and columns ir1 and ir1+1 (vy, vy+src1_col_stride).
